A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same TF-HNN research. Their complete main texts, equations, figures, tables, and appendices support reliable comparison, including matching retained material across pagination changes.

before.justification: v4 reports original TF-HNN node-classification and hyperlink-prediction results, training times, and ablations in Section 6 and Appendix J.

after.justification: v5 retains those original experiments and adds APPNP comparisons, Yelp evaluation, parameter-removal experiments, sensitivity analyses, and computational-cost measurements.

M1.justification: The TF-HNN procedure remains unchanged: fixed linear message passing with the weighted clique-expansion operator is precomputed before training the task-specific module. Equations (1) and (4)–(6) retain the same operations. New explanations and baseline ablations do not establish a modification to TF-HNN.

E1.justification: Appendix P and Table 18 add node classification on the Yelp hypergraph. The seven original hypergraphs and both existing tasks remain. This extends the evaluated data by one benchmark without introducing a new task; the added sensitivity and timing experiments use retained datasets.

E2.justification: Tables 15–16 newly compare against APPNP with the clique expansion from Equation (5) on Cora-CA and Citeseer. Table 17 also evaluates parameter-free variants of four existing baselines. The original HNN, SGC/SIGN, and appendix HyperGCL/HDSode comparisons are retained; those appendix baselines are not new additions.

E3.justification: v5 adds procedures measuring complete grid-search runtime and preprocessing separately, plus paired validation/test evaluations across hyperparameter combinations. The retained experiments keep their 50%/25%/25% splits, accuracy/AUC metrics, and negative-sampling settings. Newly documented search ranges and final configurations do not establish changes to the earlier experiments.

E4.justification: Appendix O tests removing only learnable parameters from four baselines on Cora-CA and Citeseer, isolating a design step not separately tested in v4. Appendix S adds extensive pairwise hyperparameter sensitivity analysis on DBLP-CA, beyond the retained depth/alpha analysis. Appendices S and V additionally investigate tuning cost and preprocessing overhead, substantially broadening the diagnostic evidence.

E5.justification: Both versions specify ten node-classification runs and five hyperlink-prediction runs and retain the same plus/minus uncertainty reporting. The additional results introduce no explicit changes to run counts, seeds, uncertainty estimation, confidence intervals, or significance testing.

E6.justification: Tables 15–21 and Figure 5 add substantial comparison, ablation, sensitivity, and timing results. For example, TF-HNN achieves 36.06 ± 0.32% accuracy on Yelp with 6.54 ± 0.96 seconds training time. Original benchmark scores are retained. Table 7 swaps the condition labels: v5 assigns average accuracy 77.02 to weighted S and 76.02 to unweighted S, reversing v4's attribution and aligning the table with the discussion.

T1.justification: Appendix T adds Lemmas T.1–T.2 and proofs connecting the clique-expansion operators, including their dependence on hyperedge size. Section 2 drops the prohibition on duplicate hyperedges, and Appendix V adds an O(m) preprocessing-complexity statement. The central propositions and earlier derivations remain largely unchanged, with several proof cross-references corrected.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same principal contributions: training-free hypergraph message passing, a unifying framework, training efficiency, information utilisation, and resistance to oversmoothing. The headline Trivago claim is unchanged. Added supporting experiments do not redefine these core claims.

C2.justification: v5 explicitly qualifies Proposition 4.1's entropy as conceptual in Section 4 and Appendix U. Appendices N and R add explanations involving information loss during learned feature projection and memory-constrained latent dimensions. Appendix Q explains zero-degree applicability, and Appendix S interprets hyperparameter interactions. The future-work discussion replaces explicit hyperedge-node importance learning with automated hyperparameter search.

D1.justification: v4 provides selected final hyperparameters but little tuning documentation. v5 adds Trivago configurations to Tables 13–14, extensive model-specific search ranges, validation-based checkpoint and hyperparameter selection, memory restrictions, and the eight-RTX-3090 setup for search timing. It also documents zero-degree handling and changes the code-access disclosure from an anonymous address to a GitHub link.

R1.justification: Section 3.1 and the new Appendix N substantially expand positioning against APPNP, explaining its relationship to GCN/PageRank and distinguishing training-time propagation from TF-HNN preprocessing. Additional references support the new discussions of entropy, tuning, datasets, and hypergraph applications; Eswaran et al. (2020) is removed. The principal change is the detailed treatment of closely related methodology.

P1.justification: The main seven-section narrative and existing appendices remain recognizable. v5 makes local paragraph edits, replaces 'model learning' with 'model training,' expands introductory explanations and cross-references, and adds acknowledgements and equal-contribution information. The substantial appendix additions mainly document new evidence and discussion rather than extensively reorganizing existing prose.

P2.justification: v5 adds seven tables and Figure 5, which presents 15 pairs of validation/test heatmaps. Tables 13–14 gain Trivago rows, and Table 7's condition labels are corrected. Existing figures and tables are retained with caption shortening, resizing, and reflow. The new comparative and diagnostic displays substantially expand the visual presentation.

improvement.justification: v5 substantially strengthens reproducibility and support for the efficiency claim by documenting search spaces and selection rules and measuring previously unreported tuning and preprocessing costs. The APPNP comparison, parameter-removal controls, sensitivity analyses, and Table 7 correction also address important evidential gaps. These gains outweigh remaining theoretical problems: the conceptual entropy qualification does not fully reconcile the formal equality claim, and the new UniGNN derivation in Lemma T.2 contains a normalization inconsistency with Appendix D.
